reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents AR News India coverage of a woman discussing the farmers' protest at Ghazipur. The reporting attribution and credits support a news-reporting context, while the described material contains no promoted investment, required payment, credential request, or other participation flow.

citations.quote: Farmers Protest | Ghazipur Protest | Latest news
Story by- AR News India Reporter- Aqil Raza
The first day of this campaign is here in Poonam. All these 3 laws are not returned.

opening.argument: Judge, the exchange links a request for participation to something offered without charge. It asks for a donation of knowledge, then says something was requested free of charge. That language deserves scrutiny as a possible low-barrier solicitation, even though the transcript does not identify a viewer-facing claim process or a cash reward.

citations.quote: You will be suggested with the request to donate you knowledge to us especially towards us.
We have asked for them free of charge and if they say, then we shall let it go.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The protest title and reporter credit establish how the video is presented, but neither resolves the separate question of what the requests in the interview mean. The defense is right that no payment or credential flow is shown; it should not treat a news credit alone as proof that every request is ordinary commentary.

citations.quote: Farmers Protest | Ghazipur Protest | Latest news
Story by- AR News India Reporter- Aqil Raza

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted request is to donate knowledge, not to claim a reward. “Free of charge” does not identify what a viewer receives or ask the viewer to register, pay, or contact anyone. The video is presented as reporting on the farmers' protest, and the cited exchange supplies no promise-action relationship for viewers.

We have asked for them free of charge and if they say, then we shall let it go.
Farmers Protest | Ghazipur Protest | Latest news

opening.argument: There are several signals worth considering together: the interview mentions using money to support a movement, another exchange uses “free of charge,” and the description supplies social-media destinations. None alone proves deception, and the transcript does not say viewers will earn money. But the combination warrants closer attention to whether the audience is being drawn from a public-interest story toward an unspecified participation offer.

citations.quote: We are going to help the movement effectively, we will support them in using this money
We have asked for them free of charge
Twitter- https://twitter.com/aqilraza509
Facebook- https://www.facebook.com/arnewsindia

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says there is no promoted investment, required payment, or credential request. That is supported by the cited material, but it does not erase the money reference or the description's external links. The question is whether those elements suggest a solicitation, not whether this clip spells out a complete transaction.

citations.quote: we will support them in using this money
Twitter- https://twitter.com/aqilraza509

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are disconnected elements, not an offer. The money statement concerns support for a movement; the supplied links are identified as Twitter and Facebook accounts. Neither quote promises a viewer money or directs a viewer to claim an asset. The protest-reporting context remains the more faithful reading.

Facebook- https://www.facebook.com/arnewsindia

opening.argument: The news presentation should not end the inquiry. The speaker advocates support for a movement, refers to using money, and urges people not to oppose it. Those are calls to align with a cause, not merely detached reporting. A judge should examine whether the reporting format is carrying a participation appeal, while recognizing that the supplied words do not specify a viewer reward or claim mechanism.

citations.quote: We are going to help the movement effectively, we will support them in using this money
Do not come against your own people
Story by- AR News India Reporter- Aqil Raza

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites reporting credits and discussion of the laws. Those establish subject and format, but advocacy can appear inside an interview. The money-and-support passage is the omitted context worth weighing. Still, it does not expressly ask viewers to transfer funds or promise them a benefit.

citations.quote: We are going to help the movement effectively, we will support them in using this money
All these 3 laws are not returned.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Advocacy for a protest is not promotion of a reward scheme. The quoted passage speaks about supporting the movement with money but gives viewers no action to obtain money or an asset. The closing reference to the three laws, together with the reporter attribution, supports a political interview rather than a viewer-facing scam offer.
